docs.title: 72 Hour Pizza Dough Mix
docs.summary: Three ingredients. 72 hours. The best pizza you've made at home. This is the exact recipe I've been making for over a decade, my 72-hour cold ferment pizza dough, pre-measured and pre-portioned in a bag.
docs.body:
Three ingredients. 72 hours. The best pizza you've made at home.

This is the exact recipe I've been making for over a decade, my 72-hour cold ferment pizza dough, pre-measured and pre-portioned in a bag. The best premade pizza dough you'll find, because it's not factory-made. It's my actual recipe, with Central Milling organic flour. Just add water. No scale. No measuring. No guesswork.

One pack makes 4 pizzas. Four 250-gram dough balls, each one perfect for a 12-inch pie. Or divide into 3 larger balls for 14–16 inch pizzas. Your call.

9 Month Shelf Life · Organic Central Milling Flour · Three Ingredients

Choose your pack

1 Pack — $29 · makes 4 pizzas · $7.25/pizza

2 Pack — $55 · makes 8 pizzas · $6.88/pizza

3 Pack — $79 · makes 12 pizzas · $6.58/pizza

6 Pack — $139 · makes 24 pizzas · $5.79/pizza — best value

Stock the freezer. Under $6 a pizza. Free shipping over $50.

Just add water

Everything is pre-measured and portioned. Pour the mix into a bowl, add 1¾ cups of water, and knead for 2–3 minutes. That's it. No scale, no measuring cups for dry ingredients, no recipe to follow. The bag is the recipe.

Why 72 hours?

Great pizza dough takes time. A 72-hour cold ferment breaks down gluten and complex sugars, making the dough easier to digest and developing the deep, complex flavor you can actually taste in the crust. It's why the best pizzerias ferment for days, and now you can do it at home, without a recipe or a math degree.

What's inside

Three ingredients. That's the whole list.

- 
Central Milling Organic Unbleached Wheat Flour — the same flour used by top bakeries and pizzerias across the country. No bleach, no bromation, no nonsense.

- 
Sea Salt — for flavor and ferment control. That's its whole job, and it does it.

- 
Dry Yeast — the slow engine that builds flavor over 72 cold hours.

No preservatives. No additives. No sugar. No malt powder, no "organic honey," no conditioners. If it's not one of those three, it's not in here.

How it works

- Pour the mix into a bowl.

- Add 1¾ cups of water and mix until combined.

- Knead by hand for 2–3 minutes until smooth.

- Cover and rest at room temperature for 12–24 hours.

- Transfer to the fridge for 2 days to ferment.

- About 3 hours before baking, divide into 4 dough balls, cover, and let rest at room temperature.

The dough does the work. You just wait. And when you stretch it, it stretches like yoga, no fighting, no tearing, no stress. That's why we call our mascot Yoga Dough.

Not just pizza

This dough makes incredible ciabatta, baguettes, calzones, pretzels, focaccia, and bread. One dough ball, infinite possibilities.

Why this exists

I invented the Baking Steel in 2012. Since then, the number one question I get is: "What about the dough?" People buy the steel, they get an incredible bake, but the dough is where most home pizza makers struggle. This pack removes the struggle. Same recipe I've used to feed hockey teams, teach thousands of live classes, and make tens of thousands of pizzas. Now it's in a bag.

Andris

- 
Makes: 4 pizzas (250g dough balls) or 3 large pizzas

- 
Just add water — no scale needed

- 
Organic flour from Central Milling

- 
72-hour cold ferment — easier to digest, deeper flavor

- 
Shelf stable — store in your pantry, 9 month shelf life

- No preservatives, no additives, no sugar

- 
Want the science behind the recipe? Read this.

Better than store bought pizza dough

If you've ever searched for the best store bought pizza dough, you know the options are disappointing, preservatives, refined flour, zero flavor. Our 72-Hour Dough Mix is premade pizza dough done right: organic ingredients, a real fermentation process, and the same recipe used by thousands of home pizza makers. It's the convenience of premade dough with the quality of homemade.

docs.summary: Bake 4 Sourdough Loaves at Once, or Two Pizzas Side by Side The Baking Steel Plus (15" x 20") is a 22-pound slab of solid carbon steel built for open baking bread and making multiple pizzas at once.
docs.body:
Bake 4 Sourdough Loaves at Once, or Two Pizzas Side by Side

The Baking Steel Plus (15" x 20") is a 22-pound slab of solid carbon steel built for open baking bread and making multiple pizzas at once. Bake 4 sourdough loaves simultaneously or two 12-inch pizzas side by side with the same blistered crusts, explosive oven spring, and even heat that made Baking Steel the #1 choice for serious home bakers and micro bakeries. Steel conducts heat 20 times faster than ceramic, delivering bakery-quality results in a home oven.

Pre-seasoned and ready to use right out of the box. Made in the USA. Lifetime warranty.

Perfect For:

- 
Micro bakers who sell bread and need to scale production without commercial equipment

- 
Serious bread bakers who want to open bake multiple sourdough loaves at once

- 
Pizza party hosts cooking for crowds — two pizzas at a time

- 
Home bakers upgrading from Dutch ovens to faster, more efficient open baking

- 
Stovetop griddle users — flip it over for smashburgers, pancakes, and quesadillas (gas, electric, and induction)

Why Is Open Baking Better Than a Dutch Oven?

Open baking means baking loaves directly on a preheated steel surface, no Dutch oven, no heavy lids, no one-loaf bottleneck. The Baking Steel Plus retains and radiates heat like a professional deck oven, giving you results that rival commercial bakeries.

A Dutch oven bakes one loaf at a time. The Plus bakes four. No heavy lids to remove mid-bake. Faster workflow. Better oven spring. And the steel is also a pizza machine, stovetop griddle, and sheet pan supercharger, a Dutch oven can't do any of that.

For Micro Bakers: Your Production Breakthrough

If you're selling bread from your home kitchen, the Plus is your secret weapon. Bake 4 loaves per steel — or use two Plus steels to bake 8 loaves at once in a standard home oven. Go from 12 loaves a day to 32+ without upgrading your oven. Faster turnaround, more sales, no commercial equipment needed.

Pair it with our 15" x 20" Bread Board — load your proofed loaves onto the board, slide them onto the steel, then use the board to cool your finished loaves. The Plus and Bread Board were designed together as the ultimate bread-baking system.

"How to fit four loaves of sourdough on one steel...or better yet, 8 at a time." — @freedom_farm_ri

What Can I Make With the Baking Steel Plus?

Bread: Sourdough, no-knead, baguettes, focaccia, sandwich loaves, English muffins — 4 loaves at once with incredible oven spring.

Pizza: Two 12-inch pizzas side by side. Same blistered, crispy crusts in 5–7 minutes — perfect for pizza parties.

Everything else: Pastries, roasted vegetables, flatbreads, cookies. Flip it over on your stovetop or grill for smashburgers, pancakes, quesadillas, and seared steaks. Works on gas, electric, and induction.

How Do I Use the Baking Steel Plus?

Place it on the middle or upper rack. Preheat for 45–60 minutes at 500–550°F. For bread, load your proofed loaves directly onto the steel and bake according to your recipe (typically 35–45 minutes). For pizza, launch and bake for 5–7 minutes. For the full step-by-step method, read our complete guide →

- 
Thickness: 1/4 inch (6.35mm)

-

- 
Material: Solid carbon steel, pre-seasoned

- 
Made in: USA

-

- 
Ships: Within 1–2 business days, free shipping in contiguous USA

-

What's Included

- Care instructions

- Access to our recipe library and free live online cooking classes

Frequently Asked Questions

What is open baking?

Open baking is a bread-baking technique where loaves are baked directly on a preheated steel surface without a Dutch oven. You can bake multiple loaves at once (up to 4 on the Plus), achieve incredible oven spring, and create blistered, bakery-quality crusts. It's faster and more efficient than Dutch oven baking.

How many loaves can I bake on the Baking Steel Plus?

4 sourdough loaves on a single Plus. Use two Plus steels (one on top rack, one on bottom) to bake 8 loaves at once. This is a game-changer for micro bakers scaling production without commercial equipment.

Is the Baking Steel Plus better than a Dutch oven for bread?

Yes, especially if you bake multiple loaves. A Dutch oven handles one loaf at a time and requires removing a heavy lid mid-bake. The Plus bakes 4 loaves at once with better oven spring, faster workflow, and no lids to manage.

What's the difference between the Baking Steel Original and Plus?

The Original (16" x 14") is ideal for home pizza makers and single-loaf bread baking. The Plus (15" x 20") is larger — designed for baking up to 4 loaves at once or two 12-inch pizzas side by side. Choose the Plus if you're a micro baker, serious bread baker, or frequently cook for crowds.

Will the Baking Steel Plus fit in my oven?

Yes. The Plus (15" x 20") fits in standard home ovens, including wall ovens. It sits on the middle or upper rack with space around the edges for air circulation.

Can I use the Baking Steel Plus for pizza?

Absolutely. The Plus bakes two 12-inch pizzas at once — ideal for pizza parties or families. Same restaurant-quality results as the Original: crispy, blistered crusts in 5–7 minutes, but with more capacity.

Is the Baking Steel Plus worth $169?

For micro bakers, it pays for itself in weeks by eliminating the Dutch oven bottleneck and dramatically increasing production. For home bakers, it's a one-time investment that replaces Dutch ovens, pizza stones, baking sheets, and griddles. Lasts a lifetime with minimal care.

How long does it take to preheat the Baking Steel Plus?

45–60 minutes at your oven's highest temperature (usually 500–550°F). This ensures the steel is fully saturated with heat for perfect crusts and explosive oven spring.

What is the Bread Board and do I need it?

The 15" x 20" Bread Board is a wooden board designed to pair with the Plus. Use it to load proofed loaves onto the steel and cool finished loaves. Not required, but it makes the workflow much easier — especially for micro bakers handling multiple loaves at once.

Do I need to season the Baking Steel Plus?

It comes pre-seasoned and ready to use. Over time, re-season by applying a thin coat of flaxseed or vegetable oil and baking at 500°F for one hour. Only needed once or twice a year.

How do I clean the Baking Steel Plus?

After it cools, wipe down with a damp cloth. For stuck-on food or surface rust, use our Cleaning Bricks. Mild soap is okay. Dry thoroughly and apply a light coat of oil. Never put it in the dishwasher.

Can I leave the Baking Steel Plus in the oven all the time?

Yes. Many bakers leave it in permanently. It acts as a heat stabilizer, improving overall oven performance and protecting the steel from rust. Just remove it when you need the space.

Can I use the Baking Steel Plus on a grill?

Yes. Preheat on a gas or charcoal grill for 30–45 minutes and use it for pizza, bread, flatbreads, or as a griddle surface for burgers and vegetables.

Does the Baking Steel Plus work on induction cooktops?

Yes. Carbon steel is magnetic and fully compatible with induction cooktops, as well as gas and electric stoves. Use it as a griddle for burgers, pancakes, quesadillas, and more.

Is the Baking Steel Plus safe to use?

Yes. Made from food-grade carbon steel with no coatings, chemicals, or non-stick surfaces. Pre-seasoned with organic flaxseed oil. Carbon steel has been used in professional kitchens for centuries.

docs.body:
"Best way to make pizza at home. Hands down." Bart

The Original Pizza Steel. Ridiculously good crust in 5-7 minutes.

The Baking Steel® Original arrives pre-seasoned and ready to use, no homework required. A 1/4-inch-thick, 15-pound slab of solid carbon steel that turns your home oven into a high-heat pizza oven. Steel conducts heat 18x faster than ceramic, giving you blistered crusts, incredible oven spring, and a crisp bottom in under 7 minutes.

Perfect For:

- 
Home pizza makers who want pizzeria-quality crusts in 5–7 minutes

- 
Bread bakers looking for bakery-level oven spring without a Dutch oven

- 
Anyone upgrading from a cracked pizza stone or flimsy baking sheet

- 
Grill cooks who want restaurant-quality pizza on gas or charcoal

Why Is a Baking Steel Better Than a Pizza Stone?

Steel conducts heat 18 times more effectively than ceramic. That means faster bake times, better oven spring, and crispier crusts, every time. Pizza stones crack and lose heat after the first bake. The Baking Steel is virtually indestructible, holds intense heat across the entire surface, and bakes multiple pizzas back-to-back with zero performance drop. It's not a comparison, it's a different category. Read the full breakdown →

What Can I Make With a Baking Steel?

Bread: Sourdough, no-knead, baguettes, focaccia, English muffins. The thermal mass gives you incredible oven spring that rivals professional bakeries — no Dutch oven needed.

Place it on the upper rack of your oven. Preheat for 45–60 minutes at 500–550°F. Launch your pizza and bake for 5–7 minutes. That's it. For the full step-by-step method with broiler tips and rack placement, read our complete guide →

Complete Your Setup

Pair your Baking Steel with our dough containers for perfect cold fermentation, and our 14-inch cherry wood pizza peel for easy launching and serving. Everything works seamlessly together for effortless pizza nights.

The Steel is Half the Equation. Here's the Other Half.

The most common question I get after someone buys the Baking Steel: "What about the dough?"

After 13 years of teaching home pizza, I built the answer. The 72-Hour Pizza Dough Mix uses the same recipe I've made tens of thousands of time, Central Milling organic flour, pre-measured, pre-portioned. Just add water. No scale, no recipe to follow, no guesswork.

The hydration level and fermentation time are calibrated specifically for a Baking Steel bake. One pack makes 4 pizzas. Shelf stable. Ships with your steel or separately.

The Original. The Legend.

This is the Baking Steel that started it all. Invented by Andris Lagsdin and launched on Kickstarter in 2012, the Baking Steel Original set the standard for home pizza-making and inspired a movement. Every Baking Steel is cut, finished, and seasoned in the USA. Built to last a lifetime.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Baking Steel?
A Baking Steel is a thick slab of solid carbon steel designed for baking pizza and bread at home. It conducts heat 20 times more effectively than ceramic pizza stones, creating restaurant-quality crusts with incredible oven spring and a crispy, blistered bottom. The Baking Steel Original was invented by Andris Lagsdin in 2012 and is the original pizza steel that revolutionized home baking.

Is a Baking Steel better than a pizza stone?
Yes. A Baking Steel conducts heat 18 times more effectively than ceramic pizza stones, which means faster cooking times, better oven spring, and crispier crusts. Pizza stones are prone to cracking and breaking, while a Baking Steel is virtually indestructible and will last a lifetime. The Baking Steel also works as a stovetop griddle, making it far more versatile than a stone.

Is a Baking Steel worth $129?
At $129, the Baking Steel is a one-time investment that replaces pizza stones, baking sheets, and griddles. It pays for itself after just a few homemade pizza nights compared to takeout or dining out (typically $15–25 per pizza). With proper care, it will last a lifetime, making it the most cost-effective way to achieve professional-quality pizza and bread at home.

Do I need to season my Baking Steel?
The Baking Steel comes pre-seasoned and ready to use right out of the box. Over time, you may want to re-season it to maintain the non-stick surface. Simply apply a thin coat of flaxseed oil or vegetable oil and bake at 500°F for one hour. This is only needed occasionally, typically once or twice a year depending on use.

How do I clean a Baking Steel?
After the steel cools, wipe it down with a damp cloth or paper towel. For stuck-on food or surface rust, use our Cleaning Bricks to gently scrub the surface. Mild soap is okay if needed. Dry thoroughly and apply a light coat of oil to maintain seasoning. Never put it in the dishwasher.

Will a Baking Steel fit in my oven?
The Baking Steel Original measures 16" x 14", which fits comfortably in most standard home ovens. It's designed to sit on the middle or upper rack with space around the edges for air circulation. If you have a smaller oven or need a different size, we also offer the Baking Steel Mini and other sizes.

Can I leave my Baking Steel in the oven all the time?
Yes. Many home bakers leave their Baking Steel in the oven permanently. It acts as a heat stabilizer, helping your oven maintain consistent temperatures and improving overall baking performance. Just remove it if you need the oven space for large roasts or casseroles. Leaving it in the oven also protects it from rust.

How long does it take to preheat a Baking Steel?
Preheat your Baking Steel for 45–60 minutes at your oven's highest temperature (usually 500–550°F). This ensures the steel is fully saturated with heat and ready to create that perfect crispy crust. For bread baking, 30–45 minutes is usually sufficient.

Can I use a Baking Steel on the grill?
Yes. The Baking Steel works beautifully on gas or charcoal grills. Preheat it on the grill for 30–45 minutes, then use it to bake pizza, bread, or flatbreads. You can also use it as a griddle surface for burgers, vegetables, and more. The steel handles extremely high grill temperatures without warping.

What can I make with a Baking Steel besides pizza?
The Baking Steel is incredibly versatile. Use it for artisan bread, sourdough, no-knead bread, English muffins, bagels, baguettes, focaccia, pastries, cookies, roasted vegetables, and more. Flip it over and use it as a stovetop griddle for smashburgers, pancakes, quesadillas, grilled cheese, and bacon. It replaces multiple kitchen tools.

How long will a Baking Steel last?
With proper care, a Baking Steel will last a lifetime. It's made from solid carbon steel and is virtually indestructible. Unlike ceramic pizza stones that crack and break, the Baking Steel can handle extreme temperature changes and heavy use. We back every Baking Steel with a lifetime warranty against defects.

Do I need any special tools to use a Baking Steel?
The only essential tool is a pizza peel to launch your pizza onto the hot steel. We recommend our 14" cherry wood pizza peel. A dough container helps with fermentation, and our Cleaning Bricks make maintenance easy. But you can start making great pizza with just the Baking Steel and a cutting board as a makeshift peel.

Is the Baking Steel safe to use?
Yes. The Baking Steel is made from food-grade carbon steel with no coatings, chemicals, or non-stick surfaces. The pre-seasoning is done with organic flaxseed oil. Carbon steel has been used in professional kitchens for centuries and is one of the safest cooking surfaces available.

Can I use a Baking Steel for frozen pizza?
Absolutely. The Baking Steel transforms frozen pizza into something that tastes homemade. Preheat the steel as usual, then place your frozen pizza directly on it. The high heat conductivity creates a crispy bottom crust that's impossible to achieve on a baking sheet. Frozen pizzas typically cook 2–3 minutes faster on a Baking Steel.

Where is the Baking Steel made?
Every Baking Steel is made in the USA. We source our steel domestically and every unit is cut, finished, and seasoned right here in America. We're proud to support American manufacturing and maintain the highest quality standards.

docs.body:
Make Full-Size 16-Inch NY-Style Pizza in Your Home Oven

The Baking Steel Pro (16" x 16" x 3/8") is a 27-pound slab of solid carbon steel built for one thing: the biggest, best New York-style pizzas you can make in a standard home oven. At 3/8-inch thick, 50% thicker than the Original, the Pro delivers maximum thermal mass, superior heat retention, and edge-to-edge performance. Preheat for 60–75 minutes at 500–550°F and bake restaurant-size 16-inch pizzas in 5–7 minutes.

Like every Baking Steel, the Pro is pre-seasoned by hand in Massachusetts before it ships. We season it so you don't have to, no smoke, no DIY, no waiting. Open the box, preheat your oven, make pizza.

Perfect For:

- 
NY-style pizza makers who want full 16-inch restaurant-size pies at home

- 
Pizza party hosts who need to feed a crowd fast

- 
Upgraders moving up from the Original who want more thermal mass

- 
Bread bakers who want maximum oven spring and crispy crusts

- 
Stovetop griddle users — flip it over for smashburgers, pancakes, and quesadillas (gas, electric, and induction)

Why Is the Pro Different from Other Pizza Steels?

The Baking Steel Pro conducts heat 20 times more effectively than ceramic pizza stones or cast iron. The 3/8-inch thickness means it holds more heat longer — so your oven stays hotter even when you open the door to launch. You get explosive oven spring, perfectly blistered crusts with leopard spotting, and a crispy bottom every single time. This is critical for NY-style pizza, where consistent high heat is everything.

Pro vs Original: Which Should I Choose?

Choose the Original (16" x 14" x 1/4", 15 lbs) if: You make 12–14 inch pizzas, want faster preheating (45 minutes), have a smaller oven, or want a lighter steel.

Choose the Pro (16" x 16" x 3/8", 27 lbs) if: You want full 16-inch NY-style pizzas, maximum thermal mass and heat retention, and you have an oven with 18"+ rack depth.

Both deliver incredible results. The Pro is for pizza makers who want the absolute best.

You'll Need a 16" Peel for the Pro

If you're making 16-inch pizzas, you need a peel that can handle them. Our 16" Pizza Peel is specifically designed to pair with the Pro. A smaller peel won't cut it — you'll struggle with launching, and your pizzas won't fit properly. Many customers buy the Pro + 16" Peel together to get everything they need in one order.

What Can I Make With the Baking Steel Pro?

Pizza: 16-inch NY-style, Neapolitan, Detroit, grandma, bar-style, and frozen pizza.

Bread: Sourdough, no-knead, baguettes, focaccia, sandwich loaves — the massive thermal mass creates incredible oven spring without a Dutch oven.

Everything else: Flatbreads, pastries, roasted vegetables, cookies. Flip it over on your stovetop or grill for smashburgers, pancakes, quesadillas, and seared steaks. Works on gas, electric, and induction.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Baking Steel Pro?

A 16" x 16" x 3/8" thick solid carbon steel baking surface designed for making restaurant-size 16-inch NY-style pizzas at home. At 27 pounds, it delivers maximum thermal mass and heat retention for professional-quality results in a standard home oven.

Will the Baking Steel Pro fit in my oven?

The Pro (16" x 16") fits in most standard home ovens. Most ovens are 18–20 inches deep, so the 16" Pro fits with room to spare. Measure your oven rack depth from front to back — if it's 18 inches or more, the Pro will fit. If your oven is smaller, consider the Original (16" x 14") instead.

What's the difference between the Pro and the Original?

The Pro is 16" x 16" x 3/8" thick (27 lbs) for 16-inch pizzas with maximum thermal mass. The Original is 16" x 14" x 1/4" thick (15 lbs) for 12–14 inch pizzas with faster preheating. The Pro has 50% more thickness for superior heat retention.

Is the Baking Steel Pro worth $179?

If you want full-size 16-inch NY-style pizzas at home, absolutely. At $179, the Pro replaces expensive pizza ovens, pizza stones, and baking sheets. It pays for itself after a few homemade pizza nights compared to takeout ($15–25 per pizza) and lasts a lifetime with minimal care.

How long does the Pro take to preheat?

60–75 minutes at your oven's highest temperature (usually 500–550°F). The extra thickness requires longer preheating than the Original (45–60 minutes), but the payoff is maximum heat retention and professional-quality crusts.

How big of a pizza can I make on the Pro?

Up to a 16-inch pizza — the same size as a large pizza at most pizzerias. This is the biggest pizza you can make in a standard home oven.

Do I need a special peel for the Pro?

Yes. For 16-inch pizzas, you need our 16" Pizza Peel. A standard 14" peel is too small to launch and retrieve restaurant-size pizzas properly.

Can I make bread on the Baking Steel Pro?

Yes. The Pro's massive thermal mass creates incredible oven spring and crispy crusts for sourdough, no-knead bread, baguettes, focaccia, and more — no Dutch oven needed.

Is the Baking Steel Pro better than a pizza stone?

Yes. The Pro conducts heat 20 times more effectively than ceramic pizza stones, resulting in faster cooking, crispier crusts, and better oven spring. Unlike stones, the Pro won't crack or break and lasts a lifetime.

Do I need to season the Baking Steel Pro?

It comes pre-seasoned and ready to use. Over time, re-season by applying a thin coat of flaxseed or vegetable oil and baking at 500°F for one hour. Only needed once or twice a year.

How do I clean the Baking Steel Pro?

After it cools, wipe down with a damp cloth. For stuck-on food or surface rust, use our Cleaning Bricks. Mild soap is okay. Dry thoroughly and apply a light coat of oil. Never put it in the dishwasher.

Can I leave the Baking Steel Pro in the oven all the time?

Yes. Many pizza makers leave it in permanently. It acts as a heat stabilizer, improving overall oven performance. Just remove it when you need the space for large roasts or casseroles.

Can I use the Baking Steel Pro on a grill?

Yes. Preheat on a gas or charcoal grill for 30–45 minutes and use it just like you would in the oven. Perfect for outdoor pizza parties.

Can I use the Baking Steel Pro as a stovetop griddle?

Yes. Flip it over and use it on gas, electric, or induction cooktops for smashburgers, pancakes, quesadillas, seared steaks, and more.

Does the Baking Steel Pro work on induction cooktops?

Yes. Carbon steel is magnetic and fully compatible with induction cooktops.

What's the warranty on the Baking Steel Pro?

Lifetime warranty against defects. If anything goes wrong due to manufacturing defects, we replace it. No questions asked.

docs.title: The Mini Griddle
docs.summary: , A polished griddle on one side. A baking steel on the other. Six manufacturing steps. Made in the USA.
docs.body:
,

A polished griddle on one side. A baking steel on the other. Six manufacturing steps. Made in the USA.

11.5" × 11.5" × 3/8" · 12 lbs · USA-sourced carbon steel · Lifetime warranty

"You get a polished steel surface with a grease channel that converts the Baking Steel into the world's best consumer cooking surface." — J. Kenji López-Alt, Serious Eats

The Mini is built the same way, same machined surface, same grease channel, same finishing process, in a single-burner footprint.

Six steps. One piece of steel.

The Mini isn't stamped or cast. It's machined. Here's what goes into making one:

1. Laser cut. Solid USA-sourced carbon steel, laser-cut to spec at 3/8" thick — 50% thicker than our Original Baking Steel, for more heat held and more heat delivered.

2. Mill the channel. A grease channel is milled into the griddle side, 1/4" deep, wrapping the entire inner perimeter. It catches fat. It defines the cooking surface. It's the detail Kenji noticed.

3. Shot blast. Both sides are shot-blasted — the baking side gets its texture; the griddle side is prepared for finishing.

4. Machine-smooth the griddle. The step nobody else does. We run the griddle side through a precision machine that removes a micro-layer of steel, leaving a surface almost like glass. That's what makes eggs slide.

5. Season. Hand-seasoned with organic flaxseed oil. Ready to cook out of the box.

6. Inspect. Box. Ship. Made in Hanover, Massachusetts. Inspected by hand. Lifetime warranty.

Pizza one side. Griddle the other.

The Baking Steel side. Slide it onto your top oven rack and preheat. Personal pizzas, flatbreads, naan, English muffins, bagels, small sourdough loaves — anywhere serious heat makes the difference.

The Griddle side. Set it over a single burner, gas, electric, induction. Smashburgers, eggs, pancakes, bacon, grilled cheese, seared steaks. The polished surface gets better with every cook.

The polished surface gets better with every cook. Keep it smooth with our Cleaning Bricks, built for exactly this.

Fits one burner. Goes anywhere, grill, campfire, tailgate. At 12 pounds the Mini holds serious heat but travels easily.

I'm a steel guy.

I built Baking Steel in 2012 from a piece of carbon steel I pulled off a pallet in my dad's shop in Massachusetts. Fourteen years later, we're still making every steel in the same family shop.

The Mini Griddle is the most finished, machined product in our lineup, the version of the steel where every step matters. I'd put it up against any cooking surface in any home in America.

My wife makes pancakes on ours every weekend. I watch and drink coffee.

Andris Lagsdin, Founder

Common Questions

How do I clean it? After it cools, wipe it down or scrape with a bench scraper. For stuck-on food or to maintain the polished griddle side, use our Cleaning Bricks — they're built for exactly this surface and keep it smooth over years of use.

How do I season it? It comes pre-seasoned with organic flaxseed oil and ready to cook. The griddle side also builds seasoning naturally every time you cook on it. To re-season once a year or so, rub a thin coat of flaxseed or vegetable oil on the surface and bake at 500°F for one hour.

Will eggs really not stick? Yes — once you're a few cooks in. The machined-smooth surface plus natural seasoning makes the griddle side as non-stick as a well-seasoned cast iron, without any chemical coatings.

Does it work on induction? Yes. Carbon steel is fully induction-compatible.

Can I leave it in the oven? Yes. It acts as a heat stabilizer for everything else you bake. Just take it out when you need the rack space.

It replaces your pizza stone, cast iron skillet, and flat-top griddle — all in one piece of steel. No chemical coatings, no warping, no cracking, and it lasts a lifetime. If you cook on a stovetop and bake in the oven, the Griddle is the most versatile tool you can own.

Can I make pizza on the Baking Steel Griddle?

Yes. Use the textured side in your oven — same heat conductivity and performance as every Baking Steel. Preheat at 500–550°F for 45–60 minutes and bake pizza in 5–7 minutes with blistered crusts and crispy bottoms.

Can I use the Baking Steel Griddle on my stovetop?

Yes. The smooth griddle side sits across two standard burners on gas, electric, or induction cooktops. Use it like a professional flat-top for smashburgers, pancakes, eggs, bacon, seared steaks, and more.

Does the Baking Steel Griddle work on induction?

Yes. Carbon steel is magnetic and fully compatible with induction cooktops.

Can I use the Baking Steel Griddle on a grill?

Yes. It works on gas and charcoal grills. Preheat for 30–45 minutes, then use either side — baking steel side for pizza and bread, griddle side for burgers and vegetables.

Why doesn't the Baking Steel Griddle have handles?

By design. No handles means easier storage (fits in ovens, cabinets, drawers), better maneuverability in tight spaces, and full spatula access across the entire cooking surface. Use oven mitts when moving it hot.

Is the Baking Steel Griddle nonstick?

It develops a natural nonstick patina over time through seasoning — just like cast iron. No chemical coatings, no PFOA, no PTFE. It comes pre-seasoned with organic flaxseed oil and gets better with every use.

Is the Baking Steel Griddle better than cast iron?

Carbon steel conducts heat 20 times more effectively than cast iron, giving you faster, more even cooking and better searing. It's also lighter pound-for-pound and heats up faster. Like cast iron, it develops a natural nonstick patina — but with superior heat performance.

How do I season the Baking Steel Griddle?

It comes pre-seasoned and ready to use. Over time, re-season by applying a thin coat of flaxseed or vegetable oil and baking at 500°F for one hour. Only needed once or twice a year. The griddle side builds seasoning naturally every time you cook on it.

How do I clean the Baking Steel Griddle?

After it cools, wipe down with a damp cloth or scrape with a bench scraper. For stuck-on food or surface rust, use our Cleaning Bricks. Mild soap is okay. Dry thoroughly and apply a light coat of oil. Never put it in the dishwasher.

Can I leave the Baking Steel Griddle in the oven?

Yes. Many cooks leave it in permanently. It acts as a heat stabilizer, improving overall oven performance. Just remove it when you need the space.

Will the Baking Steel Griddle fit over two burners?

Yes. At 14" x 18", the Griddle spans two standard stovetop burners comfortably on gas, electric, or induction cooktops.

docs.title: Why does my Pizza Stone Crack and How to Prevent it
docs.summary: This post exists because of a question I get all the time: "Why did my pizza stone crack?" The truth is, it's not your fault. Pizza stones are fragile.
docs.body:
This post exists because of a question I get all the time: "Why did my pizza stone crack?" The truth is, it's not your fault. Pizza stones are fragile. They're susceptible to thermal shock, they absorb moisture, and they can't handle the high heat required for great pizza. I created the Baking Steel after cracking one too many pizza stones myself. I knew there had to be a better way. Steel is virtually indestructible, it conducts heat 20x better than ceramic, and it creates a crispy, blistered crust that stones can only dream of. This isn't just a replacement for your pizza stone. It's an upgrade.
Too Lazy to read it all? Buy a Baking Steel Now!

Top Reasons Why Pizza Stones Crack
1. PUTTING A COLD BAKING STONE INTO A HOT OVEN
When you throw a cold pizza stone into a hot oven, your stone experiences the dreaded "thermal shock," which basically means your stone can't handle large temperature changes. Since it's usually made of ceramic, that can cause a fracture in the stone. Sometimes it's evident immediately. Other times it lies dormant until your next baking session.
2. ALLOWING MOISTURE INTO THE BAKING STONE
You should never wash your baking stone, because if the stone isn't allowed to dry appropriately before the next baking session, it can weaken the stone. Also, contrary to some old-wives' advice out there on the interwebs, never oil your baking stone. That's a one-way ticket to Cracksville.
3. PLACING COOL OR COLD FOOD ONTO THE BAKING STONE
Even if you've pre-heated your stone, you want to be careful about placing cool pizza dough onto it. And especially be cautious with placing frozen pizza dough on there. That'll rock your stone quicker than you can say "thermal shock.'
4. HANDLING THE STONE TOO MUCH
Even though with a name like "stone," you may expect your baking stone to be tough as nails, it's really much more fragile than you may think. Repeated handling of the stone can weaken its internal integrity over time. And, of course, the results don't show up until you're in the middle of baking that perfect pizza with company on the way. It's just how the world works, right?
5. REMOVING THE STONE TOO SOON FROM A HOT OVEN
Just like throwing a cold pizza stone into a hot oven can shock the senses out of it, pulling it out of a hot oven and setting it on the stove to cool can have a similar impact. It's just not ready for that kind of sudden temperature change.
6. USING TOO MUCH HEAT
This is a really unfortunate one, because the hotter you can get your oven, the quicker your pizzas will bake. And, you'll get that perfect crust. There's a reason wood fire ovens get up to 800 degrees! You need heat to turn out the perfect pizza! The bad news for your baking stone, though, is when you start to crank up the heat, you run the risk of shattering it into a few interestingly-shaped pieces.
Instead of being so negative, though, let me spell it out for you in positive terms how you should treat your pizza stone.

How To Prevent Your Pizza Stone From Cracking In The Future

Keep your Pizza Stone in your oven all the time. If you like a pretty looking stone, cover with foil so drips from other things don't stain it.

Always put a Pizza Stone into a cold oven and do a long pre-heat.

Minimize handling. Moving in and out of the oven can cause cracking.

Handle carefully. Any kind of drop will cause fractures.

Avoid washing or oiling a Pizza Stone. The moisture can cause it to crack.

Use only dough that is room temperature or warmer. (Some have even suggested warming it slightly on the stove top before placing it on the stone.)

Wait until the Pizza Stone is completely cold before removing it from oven.

Don't put frozen pizzas on your pizza stone. Ever.

Use a folded towel and place on the counter before you take the stone out of the oven, so the counter won't send your stone into "thermal shock."

Don't use high heat with it. (This one's kind of a bummer, since high heat makes unbelievable pizza pies!)

If you leave your Pizza Stone in the oven, remove it for the self-cleaning cycle. With the drastic temperature changes, you're asking for trouble.

Are Pizza Stones Worth This Kind Of Kid-Glove Treatment?
If you've made pizzas on your baking stone, you'd probably answer with a hearty, "yes." You're a die-hard fan. Let's face it, pizza stones work pretty well. They have quite a bit more thermal mass than a baking sheet, so they store and distribute heat better than a flimsy metal pizza pan. (That "thermal mass" part is pretty important. That's where the magic happens.) The stone gets about as close to the the results of cooking a pizza in a brick oven as you can reasonably get, and usually gives you a decent looking crust and a nice tasting pie.
Make Even Bake Better Pizzas And Never Face A Fractured Stone Again
So, here's where the news goes from kind of bad to unbelievably good. Several years back, Modernist Cuisine published some findings from their research that if you wanted to make truly amazing New York Style pizza at home, you should skip the ever-present baking stone, and opt for baking your pizzas on a piece of steel. Steel has many times more thermal mass than a ceramic stone, which means it retains heat way better than a simple baking stone and does all the stuff that makes great pizza great. Plus, it's practically indestructible. I mean, you could probably crack it with some sort of anti-aircraft missile or a near-proximity nuclear detonation, but you shouldn't be cooking with that kind of stuff anyway.
Since we love making amazing pizzas, and we hate cracking pizza stones, we went looking for someone making a baking steel, and couldn't find anyone. So, we made it ourselves. Now, we're excited to help other pizza enthusiasts make the best pizzas of their lives at home with the Baking Steel. The Baking Steel is being snapped up all around the world by novices and pros alike, and the positive reviews for it have been truly overwhelming. You owe it to yourself to at least see what you may be missing by simply replacing that cracked pizza stone. We're pretty sure you'll never want to buy another stone again.

Why do pizza stones crack?

Pizza stones crack from thermal shock—a rapid change in temperature. This happens when you put a cold stone in a hot oven, put cold food on a hot stone, or expose it to moisture. The ceramic material can't handle the stress and fractures.

Can you leave a pizza stone in the oven all the time?

Yes, but you risk cracking it if you forget to remove it during the self-cleaning cycle or if you spill something on it. A Baking Steel can be left in the oven 24/7 and acts as a heat sink, regulating your oven's temperature.

What's the difference between a pizza stone and a baking steel?

A pizza stone is made of ceramic and is fragile. A baking steel is made of solid steel and is indestructible. Steel conducts heat 20x better than stone, resulting in a crispier crust and faster cooking times.

Can I put a pizza stone in a hot oven?

No, this is the #1 cause of cracking. Always put a cold pizza stone in a cold oven and preheat them together.

How do you prepare a new pizza stone?

You don't need to season a pizza stone. Just wipe it with a damp cloth and let it dry completely before first use. Never wash it with soap or oil it.

What's the best pizza stone for an oven?

The best surface for making pizza in an oven isn't a stone—it's a Baking Steel. It's more durable, conducts heat better, and produces superior results. If you must use a stone, choose one that's at least 1" thick.

Why did my pizza stone crack in the oven?

It likely experienced thermal shock. This could be from preheating the oven without the stone, placing a cold pizza on the hot stone, or moisture getting into the stone.

Can you repair a cracked pizza stone?

No, a cracked pizza stone is a goner. The crack will continue to expand with each use. It's time for an upgrade to steel.

What's better: a pizza stone or a pizza pan?

A pizza stone is better than a pan because it retains more heat. But a Baking Steel is better than both, with 20x the heat conductivity of a stone.

Can you use a pizza stone on a grill?

Yes, but you risk cracking it from the direct, high heat of the grill. A Baking Steel is a much better option for grilling pizza.
